title: Lānaʻi Kōele project district zoning and conditions
summary: On Oct. 21, 2026, the committee approved the zoning bills for Lānaʻi Project District 2, Kōele, 8 to 1, after voting 5 to 4 to strike condition 9, the bypass road requirement. It also added water use reporting to the Lānaʻi Planning Commission, with a time limit. The landowner says the plan shrinks the district by 8% and lowers density, and Planning supports it.

timeline.text: In an 8 to 1 roll call vote, the committee approved the main motion as amended.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: Members voted 5 to 4 to strike condition 9, the bypass road requirement.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: Planning said future build-out needs a phase two approval from the Lānaʻi Planning Commission, which is when more reporting could be added.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: The chair said Planning called a five-year period typical and consistent with past conditions.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: A motion was made to limit quarterly water use reports for Lānaʻi Project District 2, Kōele to five years.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: Planning said a road built by the landowner and turned over to the County could be considered later in another project.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: The landowner said the old bypass road route would affect at least 50 or 60 homes.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: The landowner said the homes already built have no income limits.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: The landowner said it would move and preserve two old homes, including the Richardson Home.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: The landowner said that without a time limit, reporting could still be going on in 100 years.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: Chair Lee voiced support for the project and the changes.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: The landowner said the plan shrinks the district by 8% and lowers density.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: A member said they will look to the chair for recommendations on a reasonable time limit for reporting.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: The second item was Bills 24 and 25 (2024) on the zoning of Lānaʻi Project District 2, Kōele.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: The landowner said its traffic study does not require the bypass road.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: The Planning Department said it supports the zoning change and amendment.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: The landowner asked the Council to put a time limit on the reporting required by condition 8.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: The landowner said the State Land Use Commission approved its district boundary amendment with six votes.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee

timeline.text: The landowner asked the committee to back the Planning Department and Lānaʻi Planning Commission on the zoning change.
timeline.body: County Council Housing and Land Use Committee
